cpm-cpc-cpa-calculator.assumptionNote: Uses the totals you enter; it does not split results by campaign, placement, or time period. For real optimisation, compare these metrics per ad set, not just account-wide.
benefits: One input, five metrics: CPM, CPC, CPA, CTR, and conversion rate together.
Compare campaigns apples-to-apples on the metric that matters for your goal.
Spot funnel leaks: high CTR but low conversion rate means a landing-page problem.
Essential for media buyers, freelancers, and anyone spending on Meta or Google ads.

faqs.a: CPM (cost per mille) is the cost per 1,000 impressions - best for brand awareness. CPC (cost per click) is the cost per click - best for traffic. CPA (cost per acquisition) is the cost per conversion - best for sales and leads. Use the metric that matches your campaign goal.
faqs.q: CPM vs CPC vs CPA - which should I use?

faqs.a: Google Search CPMs are often $20-40+, Meta/Facebook $5-15, and display networks $1-5 - but it varies wildly by country, audience, and season. India and Gulf markets are typically cheaper than the US and UK. Benchmark against your own history, not a global average.

From the same numbers: CPA = CPC / conversion rate. A $0.25 CPC with a 5% conversion rate gives a $5 CPA. So you can lower CPA either by cutting CPC (cheaper clicks) or by raising conversion rate (better landing page) - usually the landing page is the bigger lever.
faqs.q: How are CPC, CPA, and conversion rate linked?

faqs.a: For display and social, 1-2% CTR is typical; for Google Search, 3-6% is common because of high intent. Low CTR usually means weak creative or wrong audience; very high CTR with no conversions means clickbait creative.
faqs.q: What is a good click-through rate?

faqs.a: Compare CPA to customer lifetime value, not to zero. If a customer is worth $50 to you, a $5 CPA is excellent. Break-even CPA = average order value x gross margin. Spend more than that per acquisition and you lose money on every sale.

Attribution windows, bot traffic, and view-through conversions inflate platform numbers. Track with UTM parameters and your own analytics, deduplicate conversions, and always sanity-check platform-reported CPA against actual revenue.
faqs.q: Can I trust the platform's numbers?

cpm-cpc-cpa-calculator.formula:
CPM = ad spend / impressions x 1,000.
CPC = ad spend / clicks.
CPA = ad spend / conversions.
CTR = clicks / impressions x 100.
Conversion rate = conversions / clicks x 100.
Example: 500/100,000x1,000 = $5.00 CPM; 500/2,000 = $0.25 CPC; 500/100 = $5.00 CPA.
howTo: Read CPM, CPC, CPA, CTR, and conversion rate - then find your weakest funnel stage.
keyFacts: CPM = cost per 1,000 impressions; CPC = cost per click; CPA = cost per conversion.
CTR = clicks / impressions; conversion rate = conversions / clicks.
CPA = CPC / conversion rate - improve either half to cut acquisition cost.
Compare CPA against customer lifetime value, not against zero.
Low CTR signals creative or targeting problems; low conversion rate signals landing-page problems.
Ad metrics vary hugely by platform, country, and season - benchmark against yourself.
